docs.title: Day 1: Mastering the Linux Environment
docs.text: Welcome to the first session. Today we move from the Mouse to the Keyboard.

docs.title: 1. Why Linux? (0:00 - 0:30)
docs.text: Linux is the standard for Bioinformatics because: * Stability: Can run for months without rebooting. * Performance: Handles 100GB+ genomic files easily. * Automation: Write once, run a thousand times.

docs.title: 2. Linux Architecture
docs.text: Linux consists of: 1. The Kernel: The brain managing hardware. 2. The Shell (Bash): Your translator. 3. The Terminal: Your window to the shell.

docs.title: 3. Navigating the "Library" (0:30 - 1:30)
docs.text: Everything in Linux starts from the Root (/).

docs.title: Essential Commands
docs.text: Command Action Example pwd Where am I? /home/harsha ls -lh List files (human readable) ls -lh data.fastq cd Change directory cd Documents mkdir Create folder mkdir my_project

docs.title: 4. File Operations (1:30 - 2:30)
docs.text:
Managing data without a mouse.

  • Copying: cp source.txt destination.txt
  • Moving/Renaming: mv old_name.txt new_name.txt
  • Deleting: rm file.txt (Careful! No recycle bin).
  • Reading: head -n 10 file.txt (See first 10 lines).

docs.title: 5. Practical Exercise (2:30 - 3:00)
docs.text:
1. Open your terminal.
  2. Create a folder named workshop_test.
  3. Inside that folder, create a file named hello.txt.
  4. Write your name inside it using echo "Your Name" > hello.txt.
  5. Check the content using cat hello.txt.
